subject: Food Science
title: Botulism
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Botulism.

hook.text: Botulinum toxin is the deadliest substance known. One gram could kill a million people. It grows in canned food.

buildup.text: Clostridium botulinum thrives in low-oxygen environments—improperly canned food is the perfect breeding ground.

discovery.text: The toxin blocks nerve signals to muscles, causing paralysis. Without treatment, breathing stops. Mortality was once 60%.

twist.text: The same deadly toxin, diluted to nanograms, is Botox—used cosmetically to paralyze facial muscles and reduce wrinkles.

climax.text: Pressure canning at 121°C for the right time kills the spores. Water bath canning only works for high-acid foods.

punchline.text: The deadliest toxin on Earth grows in a jar. Proper canning saves lives.

quiz.question: Why does botulism often involve canned food?
options: C. botulinum thrives in the low-oxygen environment of sealed containers
